newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper settles higher after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper settles higher after choppy session.

text.p: COMEX copper settled higher after another volatile session which opened strongly but later fell to more than a two-week low before finding some support, tradbers said.
The market welcomed a 2,100-tonne drop to 273,675 tonnes in LME stocks Friday, when a rise had been expected. COMEX stocks fell Friday by 501 short tons to 22,603 short tons.
David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said the market was looking for strong evidence - primarily from higher stocks - that copper was moving into a decisive surplus.
"With supplies still relatively tight, I think there will be a limited downside unless there was a significant influx of stocks into the LME," Rinehimer said.
December COMEX settled 0.80 cent up at 89.80 cents per pound, traded 90.75 to 88.30 cents. Spot September was 0.55 cent higher at 90.45 cents.
Volume was estimated at 9,000 lots, half Thursday's official heavy 18,473 lots.

Last Friday the market powered 4.55 cents higher only to plummet to close lower a week later than before the rally as follow-through support failed and prices succumbed to technical selling accelerated by delta hedging on LME.
